text: Psychological integration has been theorized across humanistic, neuroscientific, phenomenological, and complexity-based traditions as a multi-level process of experiential coordination, yet empirical operationalizations of integration as a structured organizational architecture remain limited. The present study introduces and validates the Self-Development Inquiry (SDi), a multidimensional instrument grounded in an organismic–transpersonal framework that models psychological functioning across structural resources (Q2), integration processes (Q1), and dysregulation-related signals (Q3).
source_label: Self-development inquiry (SDi) scale: a process-oriented measure of psychological integration in an organismic-transpersonal framework
